fixed: Two people at the table were small in the wide shots. Most shots of the two of them are now closer, from the head to the table top, and the wide shot is kept for the opening, the walk in and the big words CHOOSE NOW.
The thought bubble lay over your face when it had two long lines. Its lines are shorter, one case at a time, and it sits beside your head above the pile of cash.
The title was cut off after two seconds when the picture changed. The opening is now one shot for the whole first line, and the title leaves by itself.
On the cut into the first rule the arms were caught half way up for one frame, stretched out to the sides. They now start as the cut found them and throw their hands up inside the shot.
A reaching hand stopped at the edge of the table, behind the balls. It now rests on top of the ball it chooses.
Slumped heads hung over the open balls, which covered the mouths. The slump is a little more upright.
I'm splitting and I promise were two shots, the first only half a second long. They are one shot, and his hand goes to his heart on the promise.
The cap sat high above the head like a bulb on the first drawing. It now comes down to just above the brows, with its peak pointing the way the face is turned.
notes: The light is a code through the whole video: warm light is the game as it is played, red light is a ball opening (what would happen, or what did). So the three rules and the two steals are in red, and the cuts between warm and red are plain cuts on purpose; the planner would rather have a fade there.

There is no music for the first 24 seconds, as the script asks: a faint room tone, a ticking clock under the rules and the promise, and two silent seconds under CHOOSE NOW. Music comes in at Here is the cold logic.
The words SPLIT and STEAL are read once, big, in the second shot. On the table the balls are small, so green and red carry it from there on.
In the rules the pile is cut in two, slides to the thief, or is gone, from one shot to the next. They are three pictures of what could happen, not one moment.
Three shots are short on purpose: If you both steal (1.5 s), the thief takes it all (1.5 s) and Two steals (1.5 s).
The thought bubbles are short notes, not the narrator's words: IF HE SPLITS, STEAL = DOUBLE, then IF HE STEALS, ZERO EITHER WAY, and over the Stranger STEAL IS NEVER WORSE.
The Stranger is alone at the table for the first seven seconds, with the left chair empty, until you walk in on Take a seat.
In the Stranger's closer shots your two balls are outside the picture.

Drawn for this video: the game-show stage, the game desk, the golden ball (shut, open on SPLIT, open on STEAL, and opening), the pile of cash and half of it, a peaked cap, a striped tie, four ways of sitting (reaching, hand on heart, hands up, slumped), thought and speech bubbles, and three sounds (a clock tick, applause, a drum roll).
The voices: the narrator a little slower than usual, the Stranger in the lively man's voice a little faster. Claude cannot hear; the ticking clock, the silence and the levels are for Biku's ears.
